specularVerdict: Partly. Every roughness/metalness/clearcoat number MATERIAL_TARGET.md assigns to props is hit exactly in the hand-authored set, and on the parked car the lobe IS visible: a lacquer band along the flank and a tinted greenhouse distinct from the body, night highlight p95 0.2269. Everything else fails the eye test. The sign face is 0.35 with clearcoat 0.9 and shows max Y 0.1166 at 4.3x its own median - no highlight. The 0.40/0.85 sign post is uniform near-black at p50 0.0068. Sunlit car body p95 0.3787 against CS2's 0.4561-0.7747; CS2 car roofs clip to 0.72-0.99, ours never exceeds 0.46. Root cause is scene environmentIntensity 0.5187: props' 1.25-1.8 envMapIntensity multipliers only reach 0.65-0.93 effective, so metal at roughness 0.40 has almost no sky to reflect. Second cause: 0 of 42 props materials carry a roughnessMap, so every highlight is a smooth wash instead of a broken glint. Third: 10 glTF prop materials never got the pass at all and sit at roughness 1.00 / metalness 1.00.

issues.description: Ten glTF-imported prop materials were never retargeted: painted_wooden_bench, metal_trash_can(+rust x2), fire_hydrant(+aged), planter_box_01, street_lamp_02(+_glass, +_bulb) all sit at roughness 1.00 with envMapIntensity 1.00, and seven at metalness 1.00 - street_lamp_02_glass is chalk metal where MATERIAL_TARGET asks 0.10/0.0. PropAssets.js:466-468 only names, sets anisotropy and registers them. They are invisible to `matstats --filter props` because GLTFLoader keeps the authored names instead of the props/ prefix, so the reported '42 materials, 19 matte' hides them; the true count is 52 with 29 matte.
issues.suggestion: In PropAssets.js at the bake site (~line 466), clone each glTF material and stamp the MATERIAL_TARGET value by name: bench/planter wood -> 0.70/0.0; trash can, hydrant, lamp post -> 0.40/0.85; street_lamp_02_glass -> 0.10/0.0; street_lamp_02_bulb -> 0.10/0.0 emissive. Set envMapIntensity to match the hand-authored props (1.25 metal, 1.5 glass). Keep the shipped ORM map as a multiplier by baking the factor into the base value, and give every one a `props/` name prefix so matstats can see it.

issues.description: Specular is numerically on target and visually absent on everything except car paint. Sign face (0.35, clearcoat 0.9, env 1.3) measures max Y 0.1166 at only 4.3x its median - a flat decal. Sign/lamp posts (0.40, metal 0.85, env 1.25) measure p50 0.0068 with p95 0.0274 - a black stick with no edge highlight. Mailbox and news box (0.35, cc 0.8, env 1.0) are flat coloured boxes. Scene environmentIntensity is 0.5187, so props' compensating multipliers land at 0.65-0.93 effective env - a metal at roughness 0.40 has half a sky to reflect.
issues.suggestion: Two moves. (1) Raise props' own envMapIntensity as an interim: metals 1.25 -> 2.2, sign/mailbox faces 1.30 -> 2.0, glass 1.8 -> 2.6, so effective env reaches ~1.0-1.35 while the scene sits at 0.52. Verify sign-face max Y climbs past 0.30 and post p95 past 0.10. (2) File docs/requests/environment.md asking for scene.environmentIntensity -> 1.0 with exposure rebalanced to hold lum_p10 at 0.010, then drop the props multipliers back to 1.0-1.5.

issues.description: Zero of 42 props materials carry a roughnessMap or a normalMap (roads has 94 and 115). MATERIAL_TARGET states the base value is what a roughness map should vary AROUND, not replace. A perfectly uniform roughness turns every highlight into a broad smooth wash - visible on the parked car, whose lacquer band is a soft gradient where CS2's cs2_05 car roofs carry hard-edged streaks clipping to Y 0.72-0.99 against ours at 0.46.
issues.suggestion: Add a cheap procedural roughness map in PropTextures.js: a 256px tri-octave value-noise tile varying +/-0.12 around the base, shared by car_paint (orange-peel), post/signal/shelter/fence metal (brushed streaks along the pole axis via anisotropic UV repeat), and sign_face (sheeting grain). One texture, four repeat settings, no draw-call cost.

issues.description: The reported night-pool number is ROI-cherry-picked. Builder claims in-pool pavement Y 0.058; measured horizontal profile across props_detail_21 at row 560 peaks at Y 0.239 on the cobble strip and 0.174 on the road, ~4x the claim, against cs2_08's road p95 of 0.210 on a WET (therefore darker-diffuse) surface. The pool boundary is also abrupt: 0.114 -> 0.017 across 40 px, a 6.7x cliff that reads as a hard rim rather than a falloff.
issues.suggestion: In PropRenderer.js scale the pool texture RGB down ~2.2x so the in-pool peak lands 0.09-0.11, and extend the baked falloff's outer 25% with a smoothstep tail so the rim fades over ~120 px instead of ~40. Re-measure the same row-560 profile and put the full profile, not one ROI mean, in the report.

issues.description: Ground cover is bimodally lit: within a single front-yard ROI in props_detail_17h5 the green pixels run p50 Y 0.0198 to p99 0.2098 (10.6x) with saturation p99 = 1.000, so isolated tufts render as hard-edged neon-lime blobs against near-black neighbours a metre away. Frame-wide the mean is correct (0.0412 vs cs2_04's 0.0446) - it is the local variance, not the level, that is wrong.
issues.suggestion: In PropScatter.js the tuft/ground-cover cards are almost certainly getting a per-instance up-facing normal while the bush cards behind them get a camera-facing one. Give every ground-cover card the same hemispherical normal blend (lerp the card normal toward +Y by ~0.6) and clamp per-instance albedo jitter to +/-15%, so neighbours shade together. Target: p99/p50 within one yard below 4x.

issues.description: Grounding and placement regressions survive in props_detail_17h5: green tufts overlap the kerb face and the paved verge on the left sidewalk (the 'no longer sprouts through sidewalks' claim does not hold at the kerb edge); two loose plank/log props lie at an angle across the lawn with no contact shadow and no soil contact; and a teal car is parked in the middle of a residential front garden behind an unbroken picket fence with no driveway or gate.
issues.suggestion: Extend the sidewalk/apron exclusion mask used in PropGround.js by one cell outward so it covers the kerb face and verge, not just the walk surface. Give the plank/log props the same contact decal every other prop gets. In PropScatter.js gate the covered_car / parked-car variant on the presence of a driveway apron footprint, the way the hydrant is gated to the kerb.

issues.description: props_night_17h5 renders 7,312,951 triangles - 91% of the 8 M budget - and props_hero_17h5 7,048,185, largely from the photogrammetry glTF props whose cluster-decimation budget (0.02 of model diagonal) is generous. Draw calls are comfortable at 1490-1596 of 2500.
issues.suggestion: Raise the default decimation cell in PropAssets.js from 0.02 to ~0.032 of model diagonal for hydrant/planter/bench, and add a second LOD swapped at ~45 m. Target 5.5 M triangles to leave headroom for traffic and effects.
